title: From Hourly Rate to GP Salary: National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates Explained
description: Convert your hourly rate to an annual GP salary using 38-hour weeks. Compare the National Minimum Wage with award rates, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026-27.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual GP salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, Medicare, and super. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual GP salary is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal minimum for award/agreement-free employees. Award rates are higher minimums set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries and occupations. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. Most employees are covered by an award, so your actual minimum rate may be higher than the National Minimum Wage. Check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Guides.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my GP salary calculation?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When calculating your annual GP salary as a casual, use the loaded rate in the formula. However, the [timesheet](/) on this site lets you check a box to add casual loading automatically – never type a rate that already includes loading. Super is paid on the loaded rate as well.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your GP Salary from an Hourly Rate

Whether you're a general practitioner, a nurse, or a retail worker, converting your hourly pay to an annual salary helps you compare job offers and plan your finances. This guide explains the standard formula, the role of the National Minimum Wage and award rates, and how to account for casual loading, superannuation, and tax.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The simplest way to estimate your annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a full-time employee, the standard week is 38 ordinary hours, as defined by the Fair Work Act. If you work 38 hours, your annual GP salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 (38 × 52).

For example, at the [National Minimum Wage](/topics/minimum-wage) of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the calculation is:
- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80
- Annual: $1,004.90 × 52 = $52,254.80

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours.

However, most Australian employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, updated after the annual wage review. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. For example, a retail employee under the General Retail Industry Award may have a higher base rate than the National Minimum Wage.

If you are award-free (no award or enterprise agreement applies), the National Minimum Wage is your minimum. But if you are covered by an award, your employer must pay at least the award rate. Always check your award before assuming the National Minimum Wage applies to your GP salary.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate, as compensation for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When calculating your annual GP salary as a casual, use the loaded rate in the formula. Our [timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add casual loading – never type a rate that already includes it.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay. From 1 July 2026, the Super Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; your employer adds it separately. For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage, the annual super contribution would be $52,254.80 × 12% = $6,270.58 (provided your earnings are below the cap).

### Tax and Medicare

Your annual GP salary is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For low-income earners, the levy may be reduced or waived if your income is below certain thresholds (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as a guide).

Using the National Minimum Wage example ($52,254.80 annual GP salary):
- Tax: $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 ($18,201–$45,000) = $4,020, plus 30% on $7,254.80 ($45,001–$52,254.80) = $2,176.44. Total tax ≈ $6,196.44
- Medicare levy (2%): $52,254.80 × 2% = $1,045.10
- After-tax income: $52,254.80 – $6,196.44 – $1,045.10 = $45,013.26

This is an estimate only. Your actual tax may differ due to offsets, deductions, or the Medicare levy surcharge. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more personalised calculation.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the National Minimum Wage: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80. After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly take-home would be approximately $1,731.28. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing salary packages.

### When the Formula Doesn't Apply

The annual GP salary formula assumes consistent hours and no additional payments. If you work overtime, receive penalty rates, or have salary sacrifice arrangements, your actual pay will differ. Also, if you work part-time or casual hours that vary, your annual income may be lower. Always refer to your employment contract or award for your exact conditions.

For more detailed information, see our [reference tables](/data) for historical minimum wages and award rates, or learn about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) to understand how salary sacrifice affects your take-home pay.

### Summary

- **National Minimum Wage** (from 1 July 2026): $26.44/hour, $1,004.90/week, $52,254.80/year (38 hours)
- **Casual rate**: $33.05/hour (including 25% loading)
- **Award rates**: Higher than the National Minimum Wage for most industries
- **Super**: 12% paid on top, up to $270,830 earnings cap
- **Tax**: 2026–27 resident rates with Medicare levy of 2%

Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to quickly estimate your annual GP salary from any hourly rate.
